`cub package install` names the Component after the package. To choose its name, run step 1's `cub installer setup` and then `cub installer upload` with `--component`. In the run of 2026-11-26 for the nginx entry, both forms created the same Units.

nextSteps.summary: No delivery run is recorded for this entry. Argo CD has not run, Flux has not run, and kubectl has not run.

commands.comment: clone the base onto a Target as a dev variant
publish the Release that the cluster's Argo CD pulls

notes: Use the Space name you chose in step 3. The upload also keeps a record of the package as a hidden Unit named `installer`. The variant does not clone it, so one publish deploys the rendered objects.

ConfigHub shows nothing when Argo CD fails to read a Release. Run `kubectl -n argocd get applications.argoproj.io` and read the Sync column, because Healthy alone is not a pass. In the walk, the Application was Synced and Healthy about 4.5 minutes after the publish, on a cluster made without k8sbot.

Make the cluster with `cub cluster up --name workshop --no-k8sbot`. That command creates two Spaces, a Target, a service account and a Trigger, opens ten ports on the machine, and installs Argo CD from an unpinned upstream manifest. Argo CD in the cluster pulls each Release from the ConfigHub server, so the cluster has to reach it.
